summary: Gilchrist's towerman spotted the burning tanker Boyd in May 1937. A 1965 survey note places its station near the tower site; no source describes the site today.

visit.trail_note: A 1965 survey description gives a narrow sand road to the top of the hill where the station is. No source says whether visitors may go there today.

events.note: Frank Fitzpatrick was towerman at Gilchrist when he reported the tanker Boyd on fire.
Tanker Boyd, loaded with gasoline, reported on fire on 29 May 1937. The Gilchrist tower first noted smoke at 7:40 a.m.
Survey station described as near the site of the Gilchrist lookout tower, on government-owned property.

evidence.supports: Towerman Frank Fitzpatrick reported the tanker Boyd on fire on May 29, 1937
evidence.quote: The tanker Boyd was reported on fire this morning, the report coming from Frank Fitzpatrick, towerman at Gilchrist.

evidence.supports: Gilchrist tower, about 22 miles from the fire, first noted smoke at 7:40 a.m. and flames broke through about 10:30
evidence.quote: From the Gilchrist tower, about 22 miles away, the smoke was first noted at 7:40 a.m. and flames broke through about 10:30.

evidence.supports: The Boyd carried gasoline and had gone aground near Brevort the winter before
evidence.quote: The Boyd, loaded with gasoline, went aground on a reef near Brevort last winter

evidence.supports: 1965 survey station placed near the site of the lookout tower
evidence.quote: STATION IS LOCATED NEAR THE SITE OF THE GILCHRIST LOOKOUT TOWER ABOUT
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1965 (LMC)
EAST-NORTHEAST OF ENGADINE AND ON GOVERNMENT OWNED PROPERTY.

evidence.supports: Route is a narrow sand road
evidence.quote: ON A NARROW SAND ROAD FOR 0.5 MI (0.8 KM) TO A FORK.

evidence.supports: Route ends at a sand road at the top of a hill, at the station
evidence.quote: THE END OF THE ROAD AT THE TOP OF A HILL AND THE STATION.

evidence.supports: Gilchrist is in Mackinac County, in the Upper Peninsula
evidence.quote: in the Upper Peninsula's Mackinac County

evidence.supports: Gilchrist was a lumber settlement, postal stop and train station
evidence.quote: Gilchrist was a lumber settlement, postal stop and train station
After the community acquired its own post office in 1879, it was dubbed Gilchrist after one of the early landowners, John Gilchrist.
By 1927, the post office closed down and there was only one general store left.

evidence.supports: Village is a ghost town along the Hiawatha Trail with a few residents and buildings that appear to be original storefronts
evidence.quote: Now alone along the Hiawatha Trail, Gilchrist only has a few people and a couple of buildings that appear to be original storefronts that have been used as residences.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources. The 1937 towerman and fire come from a newspaper quote on the Forest Lookouts page, not from the newspaper itself. The fate (tower gone by 1965) is an inference from 'near the site of' wording and is worded that way in the story. No build date, height, agency or current access was found. The NGS sheet's directions to the hilltop may be out of date.
